'''Freimut Börngen''' ({{IPA|de|ˈfʁaɪmuːt ˈbœʁŋən|lang}}; 17 October 1930 – 19 June 2021) was a German [[astronomer]] and a prolific [[discoverer of minor planets]].<ref name="springer" /> A few sources give his first name wrongly as "Freimuth". The [[Minor Planet Center]] credits him as '''F. Borngen'''.

He studied galaxies with the [[Schmidt telescope]] at the [[Karl Schwarzschild Observatory]] in [[Tautenburg]], Germany. In 1995 he retired, but continued to work as a freelancer for the observatory. As a by-product of his work, he discovered numerous [[asteroid]]s (519, {{As of|2006|alt=as of July 2006}}). The research on asteroids had to be done in his spare time, as the search for small objects was not considered prestigious enough by the [[East Germany|GDR]] research managers. During the GDR regime, Börngen restricted himself to politically neutral names for his asteroids, such as topics related to [[Thuringia]] or famous scientists and [[composer]]s. Examples include [[2424 Tautenburg]], [[3181 Ahnert]], [[3245 Jensch]], or [[3941 Haydn]]. After the [[German reunification]], he chose systematically historical, cultural, scientific and geographical namings, and at times honored amateur astronomers. Other names include references to resistance fighters against the [[Nazism|Nazi]] suppression, or document a religious interest.<ref>As, ''e.g.'', in naming Asteroid [[12694 Schleiermacher]] after German theologian [[Friedrich Schleiermacher]].</ref>

Freimut Börngen achieved great reputation in the international scientific community for his human qualities and the well-substantiated choice of names. In 2006, he was awarded the ''[[Bundesverdienstkreuz]] am Bande'' (Cross of Merit on ribbon) by German Federal President [[Horst Köhler]].

The main-belt asteroid [[3859 Börngen]], discovered by astronomer [[Edward Bowell]] at the U.S. [[Anderson Mesa Station]] in 1987, was named in his honor.<ref name="springer" /> The naming and its citation was proposed and written by his colleague [[Lutz Schmadel]], and published on 20 February 1989 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 14207}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />

Freimut Börngen died on 19 June 2021 at the age of 90.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Griesser |first1=Markus |title=Freimut Börngen ist gestorben |journal=ORION |date=22 June 2021 |url=https://orionmagazin.ch/ereignisse/freimut-boerngen-ist-gestorben/ |access-date=27 June 2021 |language=de-DE |archive-date=27 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210627043450/https://orionmagazin.ch/ereignisse/freimut-boerngen-ist-gestorben/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== List of discovered minor planets ==
